description: Authored map for the admission of the candidate pack research/heterodox-thought by scripts/heterodox-admission.ts. It applies the maintainer's decisions of 2026-11-01 on the open questions (1–16, all as recommended) and on the cross-family check (items 1–11), both recorded in review/heterodox-thought-pack-2026-10-31.md. Every decision, correction and hold here carries its reason. Record IDs are not reader-facing.
snapshotDescription: Rows added and changed by the admission of the candidate pack research/heterodox-thought (scripts/heterodox-admission.ts, review/heterodox-admission-2026-11-01.md). Removing the added rows and restoring the changed ones reproduces the dataset as it was at baseCommit.
scope: The machine-succession admission (2026-11-01) adds the collection on machine succession, scale and acceleration, 1979–2026: texts that state, contest or bear on ten propositions about machines succeeding humans, the scale and setting of machine intelligence, and capital, values and acceleration, with the texts and authors they name; every record is a seed with machine-checked evidence.
rules: Open question 1: the reader-facing title is neutral and names the subject; the research directory keeps its name.

Open question 2: dataset documents (Moravec 1979 and 1989, Vinge 1993, Hanson 1994, Chalmers 2010) are recorded on the new W propositions; no dataset document is re-recorded on a concept where the dataset already records it.

Open question 3 and check decision 3: a capture that the cross-family check compared and found to hold a record's quoted wording attests that wording from the capture's date; the earliest located roles are then recomputed mechanically from the wording dates, and each change is a correction.
Open questions 4–6 and check decisions 1–2: see newClaims, hold and captures.
Open question 7 and check decision 8: a post signed “Old Nick” is credited to its signature, not to Land.
Open question 8: the second part of Lê's conversation with Land stays out (removed at integration).
Open question 9: pseudonymous and collective bylines are recorded as their bylines show; no pseudonym is joined to a legal name except where the text itself does, and then only in that text's record.
Open question 10: Andreessen's list is a cites link; the only explicitly_credits link is xenogothic 2023 to Land.

Open question 11: a person entity is created for a pack author whom an admitted link names (Nick Land, through the explicitly_credits link); a link whose target would be a new entity only for that link is held and its target listed in the search note. Links that cite a person are held: `cites` takes a document object, so they need a schema decision (see citesPersonHold).
Open questions 12–14: kept as recorded; the gaps are stated in the search note, not padded.

Open questions 15–16 and check decisions 3 and 11: the adjacent strands are listed as searched and not included, within the bounds of each search; the unread earlier texts and Drexler's chapter are listed in review/thought-spine-leads.md.

W05.criterion: Machine intelligence could come to exceed human intelligence or overall cognitive capacity not moderately but by many orders of magnitude (a factor stated as trillions, or comparable to the gap between humans and much simpler organisms or matter). Capacity here means intelligence or overall cognitive capacity, not a robot's sensorimotor or output capacity.
W05.reason: Check decision 6: the criterion is clarified; item 97 (Moravec 1989) stays bears-on.

W07.withheld: By the maintainer's decision of 2026-11-01, Land's post “Pythia Unbound” (11 September 2013) is the earliest located articulation; a cross-family check read it in an archive capture of 14 September 2013. Its quotation could not be matched again when the collection was admitted, so the post is not recorded yet, and no text holds the role until it is.
